---
title: Build on Marfa
description: Build an app, an agent or a connector that reads and writes your data with a key of its own.
---

Marfa keeps what you save. Your app, agent or connector reads and writes it through the API with a key, and sees only what that key allows. A tutorial takes you through one complete piece of work, and each guide does one task.

<Cards>
  <Card title="Build an app with Swift" href="/build/swift-app">An iPhone and Mac app that lists your notes and keeps working offline.</Card>
  <Card title="Build a connector" href="/build/connector">A program that brings records from another service into Marfa.</Card>
  <Card title="Build a Raycast extension" href="/build/raycast-extension">A command that saves an item to your instance, with a key that reaches only notes.</Card>
  <Card title="Give an agent your data" href="/build/ai-agents">A key of its own, so an AI agent works with your notes and nothing else.</Card>
  <Card title="Define a type" href="/build/define-a-type">Register a type for items no shipped type fits.</Card>
  <Card title="Keep a copy in sync" href="/build/keep-in-sync">Follow the event stream so a copy of your data stays current.</Card>
</Cards>

Looking something up? The [Catalog](/catalog) lists the types, edges, events and permissions Marfa ships, and the [Reference](/reference) covers the HTTP API, the CLI and the SDKs. To run an instance rather than build on one, go to [Run](/run).
